NC-State.essence: A near-total portal rebuild — 10 transfers around one returner (McNeil). It's a guard-heavy, three-point-driven roster: two lead-guard scorers, an elite movement shooter on the wing, and a rebounding center. Lots of perimeter shot-making, real questions about size, interior defense, and who controls the ball.

positives.b: Three 39%+ shooters in the starting group — Edmead (38.7%), Hammond (39.3%), McNeil (42.7%). You cannot sag off this perimeter, which opens driving lanes and cleans up Evans' interior looks.
Four double-digit scorers (Edmead 16.1, Hammond 15.6, McNeil 13.8, Evans 12.1), and two guards who can both run an offense (Edmead 4.4 apg). No single point of failure on offense.
The one holdover — a low-usage (0.8 apg), knock-down 42.7% sniper who plays within himself. The perfect release valve on a roster of new, ball-hungry guards.
Evans (8.7 reb) gives the group a glass presence and a rim to throw it to.

flaws.t: Two alpha lead guards, one ball
flaws.b: Edmead was the guy at Hofstra (16/4.4); Hammond was the guy at Santa Clara (15.6). Playing them together is a usage collision — someone has to accept a secondary role, and neither has had to.
A two-small-guard backcourt is a defensive target, and behind Evans the frontcourt leans on Jurkovic, a complete unknown (no stats). No shown rim protection — the paint is the soft spot.
Ten new pieces under a first-time-ish staff. This roster's floor is chemistry, and it hasn't played a game together.

bench.helps: Eemeli Yalaho is the key reserve — a stretch-4 (10.1/5.7, 39.8% 3P) who keeps the floor spaced when a starter sits. Darius Adams (Maryland, 10.8) is instant bench scoring. RJ Keene is a glue wing — rebounds (4.6) and defends in real minutes.
bench.hurts: Comeh Emuobor produces (9.0) but at 10.7% from three he shrinks the floor — a spacing liability in shooting lineups. After the top 8, it's freshmen and JUCO (Wilkins, Hall, Whitty) — unproven, with a steep quality drop.

second_unit.strength: A Yalaho–Adams–Keene trio actually preserves the identity — shooting (Yalaho), scoring (Adams), and defense/rebounding (Keene). You don't fall apart when the starters rest.
second_unit.weakness: No backup rim protection and a hard cliff after those three. Frontcourt foul trouble is dangerous, and any Emuobor-heavy bench group loses the spacing that makes this team work.

coach.might: Gainey may just lean into the guards — Edmead + Hammond together, play fast, let three shooters fire, and ride a tight 7–8 man rotation (starters + Yalaho/Adams/Keene).
should: Weaponize the spacing: pair the guards + McNeil with Yalaho at the 4 for five-out looks and use Evans purely as a roll-and-rebound anchor.
Resolve the guard conflict: anoint Hammond as the lead (higher grade, more efficient) and cast Edmead as a scoring off-guard, so it's complementary creation, not a turf war.
Defend by committee — there's no stopper, so switch, and hide the smaller guard while McNeil/Keene take the tough wing.
Protect the interior: develop Jurkovic and a young big now, because one Evans injury or foul-out exposes the roster's thinnest spot.
